**Para que serve esta vista.** Antes de:
**What this view is for.** Before isolating a system, it is worth seeing how they occupy the same space. Much of clinical reasoning is precisely about neighborhood: pain that comes from one organ and is felt somewhere else, a structure that compresses its neighbor, an exam that crosses several systems at once.

**How to use it.** Turn layers on and off to see what lies underneath. Muscles start turned off on purpose — when on, they hide everything.

**An idea that runs through every system.** Form and function go together: almost every anatomical peculiarity you will find exists because it solves a functional problem, and that is what makes anatomy stick in memory instead of becoming a list.

Sustentação, proteção, alavanca do movim: Support, protection, leverage for movement and calcium reserve.
**Quatro funções ao mesmo tempo:** suste:
**Four functions at once:** it supports the body against gravity, protects viscera (skull, rib cage, vertebral canal), serves as a lever for muscle and is the body's **calcium reservoir**.

**Bone is living tissue.** It remodels throughout life: osteoclasts resorb, osteoblasts form. This balance is regulated by PTH, vitamin D and calcitonin — and it is what breaks down in osteoporosis and renal bone disease.

**Why this shows up in the clinic.** Bone responds to load: immobilization and absence of weight-bearing lead to loss of mass. The same logic explains why weight-bearing exercise is part of osteoporosis prevention.

**On imaging.** Bone is the spatial reference of any radiograph — counting ribs and vertebrae is how the level of a finding is described.
Onde os ossos se encontram: mobilidade c: Where bones meet: mobility with stability.
**O dilema de toda articulação** é conci:
**The dilemma of every joint** is reconciling mobility and stability — the more of one, the less of the other. The shoulder is the extreme example: it is the most mobile joint in the body, and therefore the one that dislocates most often.

**Articular cartilage has no blood vessels or nerves.** It is nourished by synovial fluid, pushed into it by movement itself. Two consequences: it barely regenerates, and prolonged immobility harms it.

**Ligament is a passive restraint; muscle is an active restraint.** That is why muscle strengthening is part of the treatment of joint instability.

**In the clinic.** Osteoarthritis is the failure of this system: joint space narrowing, subchondral sclerosis, osteophytes and cysts — the four signs sought on radiographs.
Converte energia química em força, movim: Converts chemical energy into force, movement and heat.
**Contração.** O potencial de ação liber:
**Contraction.** The action potential releases calcium from the sarcoplasmic reticulum; calcium unblocks the interaction between actin and myosin; myosin pulls actin, consuming ATP. Without ATP there is no relaxation — this is what explains rigor mortis.

**Fiber types.** Slow fibers (type I) are fatigue-resistant and use aerobic metabolism; fast fibers (type II) generate high force for a short time. Training shifts the proportions.

**Muscle is also a metabolic organ:** it is the largest site of insulin-stimulated glucose uptake, which links muscle mass to glycemic control.

**In the clinic.** Extensive muscle injury releases myoglobin and potassium — rhabdomyolysis, which threatens the kidney. And muscle pain is a common complaint with statins, which makes the physical examination of this region worth more than it seems.
Bomba, tubos e volume — leva oxigênio a: Pump, pipes and volume — delivers oxygen to every cell and removes CO₂.
**A equação que organiza tudo:** débito:
**The equation that organizes everything:** cardiac output = heart rate × stroke volume. And stroke volume depends on three things — **preload** (how much the ventricle fills), **contractility** (the force with which it ejects) and **afterload** (the resistance against which it ejects). Almost all reasoning about heart failure and shock is resolved by asking which of the three is altered.

**Two circulations in series.** The pulmonary circulation is low-pressure and receives the entire output; the systemic circulation is high-pressure and distributes it in a regulated way. Left-sided failure congests the lungs; right-sided failure congests the periphery and the liver.

**The coronary arteries fill in diastole**, not in systole — the heart is the only organ that is perfused when it relaxes. That is why tachycardia, which shortens diastole, worsens ischemia.

**On imaging.** The cardiac silhouette on the radiograph and the pattern of pulmonary congestion are the first signs that the pump is not keeping up.
Filtra o plasma e regula volume, eletról: Filters plasma and regulates volume, electrolytes, pH and blood pressure.
**O rim não é só um filtro.** Ele filtra:
**The kidney is not just a filter.** It filters about 180 liters per day and reabsorbs more than 99% — urine is what is left. It is this selective reabsorption that allows volume, sodium, potassium, calcium and pH to be regulated independently.

**Three endocrine functions** that show up on exams and explain symptoms: it produces **erythropoietin** (hence the anemia of chronic kidney disease), activates **vitamin D** (hence renal bone disease) and secretes **renin**, initiating the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system that sustains blood pressure.

**Kidney injury is classified by location:** prerenal (too little blood arrives), renal (the parenchyma is diseased) and postrenal (the outflow is obstructed). This division guides the entire initial workup.

**On imaging.** Perirenal fat is what makes the kidney outline visible on noncontrast CT.
Troca gasosa, e o principal regulador rá: Gas exchange, and the main rapid regulator of pH.
**Duas funções separadas.** *Ventilação*:
**Two separate functions.** *Ventilation* is moving air; *gas exchange* is passing oxygen into the blood and removing CO₂. They fail in different ways, and arterial blood gas analysis is what distinguishes them: CO₂ retention points to a ventilation problem; hypoxemia with normal or low CO₂ points to an exchange problem.

**Ventilation/perfusion ratio (V/Q).** A ventilated but unperfused alveolus is dead space — that is what happens in thromboembolism. A perfused but unventilated alveolus is shunt — that is what happens in pneumonia and atelectasis. Shunt responds poorly to supplemental oxygen; this is the classic trick question.

**pH control.** The lung adjusts CO₂ within minutes, the kidney adjusts bicarbonate over days. That is why respiratory compensation is fast and metabolic compensation is slow.

**Surfactant** reduces surface tension and prevents alveolar collapse — its deficiency defines hyaline membrane disease of the premature infant.
Recebe, integra e responde — em milisseg: Receives, integrates and responds — in milliseconds.
**Divisão que orienta o exame.** Central:
**A division that guides the examination.** The central system (brain and spinal cord) integrates; the peripheral system conducts. The autonomic system works without voluntary command, divided into sympathetic (fight or flight) and parasympathetic (rest and digest).

**The brainstem concentrates vital function** in a minimal space: cranial nerve nuclei, respiratory and cardiovascular centers, and the long tracts that ascend and descend. That is why a small lesion there produces a disproportionate deficit, and why herniation is fatal.

**Localize before naming.** Faced with a deficit, the question is where the lesion is, not what the disease is: hemisphere, brainstem, spinal cord, root, nerve or muscle. Each level has an examination signature.

**The brain does not store energy.** It depends on a continuous supply of glucose and oxygen, which explains how quickly ischemia causes irreversible damage — the basis of urgency in stroke.
A superfície onde a função vira territór: The surface where function becomes territory.
**Função tem endereço.** Áreas motoras p:
**Function has an address.** Primary motor areas in the precentral gyrus, sensory areas in the postcentral gyrus, visual in the occipital lobe, auditory in the temporal lobe. The homunculus distorts proportions according to innervation density — hand and face occupy territory out of proportion to their size.

**Hemispheric dominance.** In most people, language is on the left: Broca (frontal) for production, Wernicke (temporal) for comprehension. That is why a left middle cerebral artery stroke adds aphasia to the motor deficit, and a right one does not.

**The folds are not decoration.** Gyri and sulci multiply the cortical area within a skull of fixed size.

**Direct clinical correlation.** Knowing the territory of each cerebral artery allows you to predict the deficit from the occluded vessel — and conversely, to suspect the vessel from the examination.
Quebra o alimento, absorve nutrientes e: Breaks down food, absorbs nutrients and processes what has been absorbed.
**Uma linha de montagem.** Boca e estôma:
**An assembly line.** The mouth and stomach perform mechanical breakdown and begin chemical digestion; the **small intestine is where almost all absorption takes place**, with its surface multiplied by folds, villi and microvilli; the colon recovers water and electrolytes.

**The liver is the mandatory filter.** Everything the intestine absorbs passes through it via the portal vein before reaching the circulation — this is the first-pass effect, which explains why certain drugs do not work orally.

**Bile does not digest: it emulsifies.** It breaks fat into droplets for pancreatic lipase to act on. Without bile, there is malabsorption of fat and fat-soluble vitamins.

**In the clinic.** Portal hypertension explains at once esophageal varices, splenomegaly, ascites and collateral circulation — four findings that seem unrelated and have the same cause.
Comunicação química lenta e sustentada,: Slow, sustained chemical communication through feedback loops.
**A lógica é sempre a mesma:** um eixo h:
**The logic is always the same:** a hypothalamus → pituitary → target gland axis, with the final hormone inhibiting the levels above. Understanding the loop solves most questions — if the target hormone is low and the stimulating hormone is high, the failure is in the gland (primary); if both are low, the failure is above (secondary).

**Nervous and endocrine systems complement each other:** the nervous system is fast and targeted, the endocrine system is slow and diffuse. The adrenal gland combines both — the cortex is classic endocrine tissue, the medulla is practically a sympathetic ganglion.

**Feedback explains the most common iatrogenic problem in this group:** prolonged exogenous corticosteroid use suppresses the axis, and abrupt withdrawal causes adrenal crisis.

**Note on these meshes.** The parathyroid glands here are position markers, not anatomical models — they are meant for localization, not for studying shape.
Camada mais interna: endotélio sobre con: Innermost layer: endothelium over loose connective tissue, continuous with the lining of the vessels. It lines the chambers and folds to form the valves — it is where infective endocarditis settles, typically on an already damaged valve.
Camada média e mais espessa: cardiomióci: Middle and thickest layer: striated cardiomyocytes joined by intercalated discs, which couple contraction electrically and mechanically. It is the tissue that dies in infarction and that remodels in heart failure. The subendocardium, farthest from the coronary arteries, is the first to suffer in ischemia.
Mesotélio sobre conjuntivo e gordura, ad: Mesothelium over connective tissue and fat, adherent to the surface of the heart — it is the visceral layer of the serous pericardium. The coronary arteries and their veins run in the subepicardial fat before plunging into the myocardium.
Espaço virtual entre as lâminas visceral: Potential space between the visceral and parietal layers, containing 15–50 mL of lubricating fluid. An effusion that accumulates quickly gives the sac no time to stretch: this is the mechanism of cardiac tamponade.
Mesotélio que forra por dentro o pericár: Mesothelium lining the inside of the fibrous pericardium. Together with the visceral layer, it bounds the pericardial cavity and produces the fluid that lets the heart glide with each beat.
Saco externo de conjuntivo denso, pouco: Outer sac of dense connective tissue, poorly distensible, anchored to the diaphragm and sternum. Its low compliance explains why an acute effusion compresses the heart even at small volumes — and why chronic effusions can reach liters without causing tamponade.
Os ramos coronários percorrem o subepicá: The coronary branches run through the subepicardium and send perforating branches into the myocardium. Occlusion of a branch kills the subendocardium first, the most distal territory of this supply.
Drena o sangue do miocárdio acompanhando: Drains blood from the myocardium, accompanying the arteries in the subepicardium, toward the coronary sinus, which empties into the right atrium.
